stem.text: Let \( w = g(t) \) be a twice-differentiable function. Suppose that \( g'(3) = -11 \). Write this statement in Leibniz notation, and state what it means.

answer_key.label: \( \left. \frac{dw}{dt} \right|_{t=3} = -11 \), so the rate of change of w with respect to t when t = 3 is -11.

worked_solution.text: In \( g'(3) \) the function is g, the independent variable is t, and the derivative is evaluated at t = 3, so the statement is about one input only.
In Leibniz notation the same statement is \( \left. \frac{dw}{dt} \right|_{t=3} = -11 \).
It says that the rate of change of w with respect to t when t = 3 is -11.

options.label: \( \left. \frac{dw}{dt} \right|_{t=3} = -11 \), so the rate of change of w with respect to t when t = 3 is -11.
\( \left. \frac{dt}{dw} \right|_{t=3} = -11 \), so the rate of change of t with respect to w when t = 3 is -11.
options.derivation: the roles of the two variables exchanged, so the derivative is read with respect to the dependent variable

options.label: \( \frac{g(3)}{3} = -11 \), so w divided by t when t = 3 is -11.
options.derivation: the Leibniz fraction read as the quotient of the two quantities at the point

options.label: \( \frac{dw}{dt} = -11 \), so the rate of change of w with respect to t, the same at every t, is -11.
options.derivation: the point of evaluation dropped, so a value at one input is read as the derivative function
